observed_discontinuity: After virtual dispatch selects java.lang.Thread.start, Frozen Bubble GameView.<init> did not return. start ran GameThread.run on the calling thread, and the shared instruction budget was exhausted inside that loop.
required_semantics: start returns to its caller after the receiver thread has been started.
run makes progress independently of that caller.
A continuous run loop does not consume the caller's instruction budget.
An exception on the worker does not become the caller's pending exception.
isAlive is true while the receiver is starting or running, and false when it is new or terminated.
join waits until a running receiver terminates.
sleep pauses only the current Java execution context.
monitor-enter excludes another execution context and allows same-context reentry.

differences.description: Before this repair, native_thread_start called dx_vm_execute_method on run and returned only when run returned. isAlive always returned false, join was a no-op, and the instruction budget and current frame belonged to the caller.
differences.relevance: GameThread.run is while (mRun). The constructor calls setRunning(true) then start. The caller stayed in run until the shared 500000-instruction budget was exhausted, so onCreate never finished and surface callbacks did not run.

earliest_evidenced_divergence: API19 Thread.start calls VMThread.create so the receiver runs on its own thread and start returns. The previous AGR native_thread_start executed run on the caller.

evidence.artifact: android-4.4.4_r2 libcore Thread.start is public synchronized void start and calls VMThread.create(this, stackSize). The method comment says the receiver runs on the receiver thread, not the thread that called start. isAlive is true once the VMThread exists. join waits for that thread. sleep suspends the current thread. A second start throws IllegalThreadStateException. Dalvik vm/Sync.cpp dvmLockObject and dvmUnlockObject own monitor mutual exclusion. GameThread.run in robinst/frozen-bubble-android GameView.java loops while (mRun), calls Thread.sleep(delay), and calls lockCanvas only when surfaceOK is true. setSurfaceOK and the game loop synchronize on mSurfaceHolder.

remaining_uncertainty: The Frozen Bubble probe is a local Linux host run. It is not Simulator discovery and not a device run.
Object.wait, notify, and notifyAll are not implemented. This probe did not call them.
Each top-level execution context uses the process watchdog of 10000 ms. That watchdog was not the stop.

load_class can hold the shared VM lock across class initialization. A clinit that waits on a monitor owned by a thread which needs that lock can deadlock. It was not observed; Frozen Bubble class init during onCreate happens before the worker runs.
System.currentTimeMillis still returns 0, so the GameThread delay stays FRAME_DELAY 40. That was not changed.
pthread_create failure sets TERMINATED and throws OutOfMemoryError. That path was not forced.
The next public stop is unresolved SurfaceHolder.lockCanvas. It is outside this contract.
next_action: Do not reopen Thread. lockCanvas ownership is framework-surface-holder-canvas.json. Do not run a Simulator for this Thread contract.
host_adaptation: DxVM keeps process-global heap, class table, statics, interned strings, GC, framework and activity roots, and a recursive shared lock. DxExecutionContext keeps current_frame, stack_depth, pending_exception, insn_count, insn_limit, the watchdog timestamp, thread-local diagnostics, and the frame pool. The current context is thread-local. Thread.start creates a joinable Darwin pthread and returns. The shared lock is not held across run. GC takes a safepoint before that lock and marks every context. Inline-cache updates take the shared lock. A Java Thread is not entered in the guest pthread table. Monitors are per object, owned by an execution context, and recursive. Shutdown sets stop_requested and joins workers before the heap is freed.
